subject: Signal intake & runbook acceptance for FinApps observability
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finapps.com>, Rajiv Gupta <rajiv@finapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Signal intake & runbook acceptance for FinApps observability

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the session last week. As discussed, attached is a compact telemetry intake and a runbook template we use for initial handoffs. Goal for this thread: agree on the set of signals we will send from FinApps, confirm tracing hooks and sampling targets, and get acceptance on the runbook so our CS and SRE teams can start dashboarding and alert wiring.

High-level checklist (proposed):
- Required signals: request latency, request success/failure, model inference duration, token-level error counts, KV cache miss rate
- Tracing hooks: add span around Redwood SDK calls, tag with request_id and customer_id
- Sampling: 5% trace sampling for production by default, 100% for errors and 10% for slow requests (>1.5s)
- Dashboards: 1) request overview, 2) error taxonomy breakdown, 3) tail-latency heatmap
- Alert routing: page on P0 errors, pager -> SRE on-call; email -> CS for repeat-rate issues; Slack #finapps-support for ops chatter
- Runbook acceptance: FinApps to confirm ownership and escalation contacts, then Redwood will import into the console and enable alerting on canary traffic

Attachments: finapps-telemetry-spec-v1.pdf (spec), runbook-template.md (editable)

Next step: Can you confirm the signal list and who on your side will own the runbook? Once we have that, Connor will do a quick instrumentation review and Marissa will schedule the CS handoff call.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@finapps.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Gupta <rajiv@finapps.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 13:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Signal intake & runbook acceptance for FinApps observability

Hi Ben / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear checklist. A few quick notes from our side after a fast sync with infra:
- We can emit the requested metrics. We currently have request latency, success/failure, and inference_duration; need help adding KV cache miss rate and token-level errors (we send a tokenized debug stream to our internal logger today).
- Tracing: we have distributed tracing via OpenTelemetry. Adding a span around the Redwood SDK call is straightforward; we just need the exact span name and tag names you expect.
- Sampling: 5% in prod sounds fair. We'll do 100% on errors and 10% on >1.5s slow requests.
- Runbook ownership: Rajiv will be the primary owner for the first 90 days (rajiv@finapps.com).

Questions:
1) What are the canonical tag keys you want for request_id / customer_id?
2) Do you expect KV cache metrics to be counters or ratios (we can emit both but want to be efficient)?

If you can provide the exact keys and a short example of an instrumented span, Connor can start the review tomorrow.

Appreciate it —
Elena
Director of Infrastructure, FinApps
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finapps.com>, Rajiv Gupta <rajiv@finapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Signal intake & runbook acceptance for FinApps observability

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks for the quick response. Short answers to your questions and an example payload below. I'll also drop a small instrumentation snippet in the shared doc.

Recommended tag keys (canonical):
- redwood.request_id
- redwood.customer_id
- redwood.model_version

KV cache: emit both a counter (kv.cache_hits, kv.cache_misses) and a derived ratio (kv.hit_rate) if possible; if cost is a concern, prioritize counters and we will compute hit_rate in the dashboard.

Example OpenTelemetry span (pseudo):
- span.name: "redwood.sdk.call"
- attributes: { "redwood.request_id": "<uuid>", "redwood.customer_id": "finapps:acct-123", "redwood.model_version": "rw-v1.2.1", "http.status_code": 200, "redwood.kv_hit": true }

I will review your current trace output and flag any missing attributes. Proposed next step: brief instrumentation review call (20 minutes) tomorrow at 11:00 PT. Does that work for you?

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Connor —

11:00 PT tomorrow works. We'll have one of our engineers (Priya) on the call to review trace exports and KV metrics. For the runbook, Rajiv will fill in primary/secondary pager contacts and acceptance criteria by end of day Thursday.

One more ask: can you include a short alert-routing matrix in the runbook that defines which alerts go to SRE vs CS vs Engineering and example thresholds? That will speed up our internal review.

Thanks —
Elena
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finapps.com>, Rajiv Gupta <rajiv@finapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Signal intake & runbook acceptance for FinApps observability

Elena / Rajiv —

Great — thanks for the updates and for assigning Rajiv. I pulled together a short alert-routing matrix and pre-filled thresholds in the runbook template (attached) based on best practices for LLM inference workloads. The key routing rules we propose:

- P0 (availability / major error spike): Page SRE on-call, notify CS + Eng. Threshold: error rate > 5% across 1 minute and sustained for 2 minutes.
- P1 (degraded latency / increased tail): Page SRE for latency > 99th percentile > 3s on >1% traffic, notify CS.
- P2 (quality regressions / model-output errors): Email CS + Eng, include sample traces; threshold: error-count increase > 200% week-over-week on a supervised metric.
- Billing/Quota alerts: Email billing ops and CS (no page).

Runbook acceptance checklist (complete these to mark runbook accepted):
1) Runbook owner and on-call contacts listed
2) Instrumentation verified (span + tags present)
3) Dashboards created and shared with FinApps (links in the doc)
4) Canary alerts enabled on 0.5% traffic for 48 hours

Action items captured:
- Rajiv: provide on-call contacts + confirm acceptance criteria by EOD Thu (noted)
- Priya: attend instrumentation review tomorrow 11:00 PT
- Connor: instrumentation review and trace attribute verification
- Marissa: import runbook and enable canary alerts once Rajiv signs off

Attaching: runbook-template.md (updated) and link to a sample dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/finapps-overview

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the instrumentation review. Happy to keep the thread for visibility.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
